audit.why: FAV / 4-10 with a 5/10 carry threat is backed by the largest sample in the slice — 53.37% over 2342 Emerald+ games — and by the kit: Locke's only mobility is a 10s blink and his kill script needs an execute threshold a full-tank Nautilus rarely sits under.
audit.corrected: No change to diff, tone, diffRating or carryRating.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer's spikes[] has three entries where four are expected, and the missing one is the Level 6 / late Purgatory threat — the single most important timing on the page. The three present spikes carry no cooldown numbers at all, which the packet flags as zero sequencing cues.
audit.why: spikes[] runs Lvl 1, Lvl 3, 2+ items and never mentions the ultimate. enemyKit R is a 120/100/80s execute that 'gains additional power for sealing away enemy champions', so his floor rises with every seal — that is a genuine late spike and it belongs in the chronological slot after 2+ items.
audit.corrected: spikes[3].text and spikes[3].when created with before:null, stating the seal-scaling execute floor and its 80s late cooldown; Purgatory's 120s cooldown added to whys[4] and Dredge Line's 14s to whys[5].
sources: packet defects: 'spikes[] has 3 entries, expected 4' and 'NO cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere'

audit.whatIsWrong: Itemization tells the player anti-heal is optional because Locke's sustain is 'self-refund, not lifesteal'. Grievous Wounds reduces healing by source-agnostic percentage — a delayed self-refund is still healing. The page also never states that a landed Dredge Line cancels Ashen Pursuit outright.
audit.why: enemyKit W: 'At the end of the duration, Locke will heal back a portion of the damage he takes during the effect' — it carries the heal flag and the missingInteractions file flags needs-antiheal for this exact pairing. enemyKit E carries the dash flag on a flat 10s cooldown, and the same file flags enemy-dash-deniable: Nautilus's hook is hard CC, so it kills the blink rather than merely beating it to the punch.
audit.corrected: report[8].t now says Grievous Wounds cuts Soul Ignition's refund heal; report[9].t states Ashen Pursuit's flat 10s cooldown and that hard CC cancels the blink.
sources: enemyKit W/E text, cooldowns and flags

edits.after: Late, Purgatory's execute floor rises with every champion he seals — deny the seals and his 80s ultimate never threatens your full-tank health bar.

edits.before: Level 6 evens out — his Purgatory execute threatens you once W fades, so stop coasting at low HP.
edits.after: Level 6 evens out — Purgatory is a 120s execute that lands once your W fades, so never coast at low HP.

edits.before: First item stays a skill window — he dodges Q and trades inside its cooldown, so hold the hook until it is guaranteed.
edits.after: First item stays a skill window — Dredge Line is 14s at rank 1 and he trades inside it, so hold the hook until guaranteed.

edits.before: Early HP and MR blunt the nail chip (his damage is AP). A stopwatch/Zhonya’s-class answer beats Purgatory outright: untargetable at the floor = execute denied. Anti-heal is optional — his sustain is self-refund, not lifesteal.
edits.after: Early HP and MR blunt the nail chip (his damage is AP). A stopwatch/Zhonya’s-class answer beats Purgatory outright: untargetable at the floor = execute denied. Grievous Wounds cuts Soul Ignition's refund heal — buy it before extended trades.

edits.before: Commit on the post-E window, on whiffed nail recasts, and with your jungler when his totem is down. Bait his answer first.
edits.after: Commit on the post-E window: Ashen Pursuit is 10s flat, and hard CC from your hook cancels the blink outright. Bait it first.
